ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A, D, B, E are on the same line, $AC=EF$, $AD=BE$, $\angle C=\angle F=90^\circ$, $\angle ABC=65^\circ$, find the degree of $\angle ADF$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AD = BE$,\\
it follows that $AD + BD = BE + BD$, which means $AB = DE$,\\
furthermore, since $AC = EF$,\\
we have Rt$\triangle ABC \cong$ Rt$\triangle EDF$ (by HL criterion),\\
which implies $\angle FDE = \angle ABC = 65^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle ADF = 180^\circ - \angle FDE = 180^\circ - 65^\circ = \boxed{115^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First look at the figure: A, D, B, E are on the same straight line, C is at the upper left, and F is at the upper right; on the left is triangle ACB, on the right is triangle DFE, and at C and F both are right angles. It is known that A, D, B, E are collinear, so AB = AD + DB, DE = DB + BE. Also because AD = BE, so AB = DE. Combining further with AC = EF, and ∠C = ∠F = 90°, it can be known that right triangle ABC and right triangle EDF satisfy HL, and are congruent. Therefore the corresponding angles ∠FDE = ∠ABC = 65°. Since A, D, E are on the same straight line, DA and DE are opposite rays, so ∠ADF and ∠FDE are supplementary angles, hence ∠ADF = 180° - 65° = 115°.
